coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 8 units (the domain directory itself plus 7 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md), 48 files total — matches the expected 8 units / 48 files exactly. Every file was read. The seven largest leaf files (05.01.01, 05.01.02, 05.01.03, 05.02.01, 05.03.01, 05.03.03, 05.03.05, 05.04.01, 05.06.01, 05.06.03) were read via section extraction that carried Overview, Behavior (all sub-headings), Happy Path, Edge Cases, States, Decisions and Open Questions verbatim with line numbers, and omitted only the Deep Think Annotations, Cross-Cut Notes and auto-generated Related Specs sections, which are rationale/link material rather than normative product statements; the Decisions tables restate every DT outcome that carries normative force. All other files were read in full. Rubric dimensions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are N/A for every unit in this domain — they are scored against meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, none of which fall inside this domain's tree. Dimensions 3, 7 and 8 are applicable to every file; applicableCheckpoints per unit = files x 3.

findings.claim: The Universal-parameters rule and D-04 contradict each other on whether a zero-cash pricing model (points, spec) must declare a minimum, currency, tax treatment and rounding rule before it can publish. The model library gives points and spec their own required-parameter sets that contain none of the four, so the publish gate for the two shapes the domain treats as thesis-critical is undefined.
findings.evidence: 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:49 — "Every model — regardless of shape — declares these before it can be published. A model missing any of them is **not publishable**; the listing cannot go live (D-03, D-04, D-05)" followed by the table rows "**Minimum**", "**Currency**", "**Tax treatment**", "**Rounding rule**". CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:186 — "| D-04 | Every cash model declares **currency and tax treatment**; every rendered figure states its tax treatment explicitly |". And 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:42 — "| **Points** | % of master and/or publishing | percentage · **asset (master / publishing / both)** | production, topline | **No — zero cash; a rights term (05.06.02)** |"; :43 — "| Spec | nothing | **trigger condition** · the term that vests on trigger · **the elected posture whose effect it defers** (05.06.01 D-14) | speculative writing/production | No — conditional (DT-10) |". D-03 at :185 restates the unqualified form: "Every model declares a **minimum**; a model without one is not publishable".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a points-only or spec listing is publishable without a minimum, a currency, a tax treatment and a rounding rule — and, if it is required, what a 'minimum' or a 'rounding rule' denotes on a percentage-of-master term.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A reads line 49 literally and blocks publish on every points-only listing because there is no minimum to enter, killing the entire points-only market the domain calls thesis-critical. Implementer B reads D-04 and applies the four universal parameters only to cash models, so a points-only listing publishes with no tax treatment — and the moment a hybrid fee+points deal renders, the fee leg has no declared tax treatment either because the model was classified zero-cash.

findings.claim: The taxonomy declares rights posture as a listing-level axis with cardinality 'Exactly 1', citing the very decision that makes the election per-tier; and 05.06.01 requires two postures (master and composition) on every tier. The three statements cannot all hold — the axis model is off by both a level and a count.
findings.evidence: 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:44 — "| Rights posture | work-for-hire · licence · co-ownership · points | `05.06.01` | Exactly 1 | Always (`05.01.01` D-02 — no default) |" (columns: Axis | Example values | Owner | **Cardinality on a listing** | Required?). CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.01-service-listings-packages-rate-cards.md:183 — "| D-02 | Rights posture is an explicit election **per tier** at publish time — no default | ... Per tier rather than per listing because tiers routinely differ in what they hand over", reinforced by its edge case at :74 — "| Seller elects posture on tier 1 but not tier 2 | Publish blocked — election is per **tier**, not per listing." AND CONTRADICTED BY 05.06.01-engagement-rights-posture.md:220 — "| D-05 | **The posture is elected per copyright**: a master posture and a composition posture, both required, on every tier."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the rights-posture facet is one value per listing, one per tier, or two per tier — i.e. the cardinality of the single most consequential field in the domain.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the listing facet model from 05.01.02's axis table creates one rights_posture field on the listing. A Producer publishes 'Mix / Mix + Master / Mix + Master + Stems' where the Mix tier licenses and the Mix + Stems tier assigns; the model cannot express it, so either the publish gate at 05.01.01:74 can never fire (there is no per-tier field to be missing) or the composition posture that 05.06.01 D-05 makes mandatory has nowhere to live and every engagement executes with an unelected composition copyright.

findings.claim: The service-mode axis is specified three incompatible ways: the taxonomy gives it three values including `hybrid` with cardinality 1..2; the axis's owning feature renders it as a single-select toggle defaulting to Remote; and that same feature says hybrid is not offered at launch and must be two separate orders.
findings.evidence: 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:41 — "| Service mode | remote · on-location · hybrid | `05.01.05` | 1..2 | Always |". CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.05-remote-vs-on-location-service-mode.md:63 — "| Empty | New listing, no mode chosen yet | Mode toggle defaults to Remote; on-location fields collapsed |" (a toggle is single-valued, and a default contradicts 'Always required'). AND BY 05.01.05-remote-vs-on-location-service-mode.md:75 — "| Hybrid | Order mixes on-location + remote stages | **Interim (launch): not offered as one unified engagement.** A buyer wanting track-on-location + mix-remote places two separate orders ... The unified hybrid model ... is an architecture decision deferred to `/create-prd` (Q-01). |"
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the listing form offers a `hybrid` mode value at all, and whether mode is a single-select toggle or a 1..2 multi-select — noting that selecting {remote, on-location} and selecting {hybrid} would be two ways to express the same thing with no stated difference.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the mode picker from the taxonomy: a required multi-select of three values. A seller selects `hybrid`. 05.01.05's cascade has no branch for it — mode determines the pricing shape, the scheduling model (queue vs calendar), the requirement set and the delivery artifact — so the engagement is created with no scheduling model and no acceptance basis, which is the exact fork 05.01.05 DT-03 says must never be treated as a filter.

findings.claim: The domain CX records CX-12 as a resolved contradiction by asserting that the capacity ceiling gates quote *issuance*. Neither feature it claims to reconcile implements that: 05.01.07 D-03 makes the ceiling gate ordering only, and 05.02.01 shows a seller with live issued quotes while already over the ceiling, with only an advisory exposure indicator at drafting time.
findings.evidence: services-marketplace-cx.md:137 — "Acceptance of a live offer always succeeds and increments the accepted-engagement count; **issuance of a *new* quote is what the ceiling blocks**. Failure surfaces at issuance (\"you're at capacity\"), never at the buyer's acceptance." CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.07-seller-capacity-queue-intake-limits.md:94 — "| D-03 | At-capacity listings stay visible and non-orderable | Delisting destroys the seller's discovery and SEO to solve a temporary state. |" (no mention of quote issuance anywhere in the file). AND BY 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:112 — "| **Seller is at their concurrency ceiling when the buyer accepts** | Acceptance is **not** blocked ... The ceiling binds *ordering* (05.01.07 D-03), not acceptance. The seller goes over ceiling and is told. | Seller: \"You're now at 5 of 4 concurrent. **Two quotes are still live** — withdraw them?\" |" — i.e. quotes were issued and remain live at or over the ceiling. 05.02.01 Happy Path step 3 (:77) provides only "their **outstanding-offer exposure** (\"3 live quotes totalling 14 days of work against a ceiling of 4 concurrent\")", an indicator, not a block.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a seller at their concurrency ceiling can issue a quote at all — a hard block per the domain CX, or an advisory exposure figure per 05.02.01.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer follows the domain CX and hard-blocks quote issuance at the ceiling. The emergency-cover shape (05.05.01, which 05.02.01 D-06 protects with a 1-hour expiry floor) becomes impossible for exactly the busy sellers who need to dep out, and 05.02.01's own edge-case copy ('Two quotes are still live — withdraw them?') is unreachable because the state it describes cannot be entered. The reverse implementer leaves issuance unbounded and CX-12's 'resolution' is a paragraph describing behaviour that does not exist.

findings.claim: 05.01.06 asserts that turnaround is a required listing attribute and cites 05.01.01 for it, but 05.01.01's enumerated publish gate and its Blocked state do not include turnaround.
findings.evidence: 05.01.06-turnaround-rush-service-levels.md:66 — "**Empty** does not occur — a listing without a declared turnaround is invalid (turnaround is a required listing attribute per 05.01.01)". NOT SUPPORTED BY 05.01.01-service-listings-packages-rate-cards.md:62 — "The publish gate runs: posture elected on every tier · required facets set · demo media transcoded or placeheld · payout account onboarded (warns, does not block). Publish is atomic (D-11)." NOR BY 05.01.01:114 — "| Blocked | Publish gate failed (missing per-tier posture / required facet / craft) | Inline blockers list naming the specific missing item and tier |". Turnaround is also absent from 05.01.02's axis table (:37-44), so it is not a 'required facet' either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the publish gate blocks a listing with no declared turnaround.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the publish gate from 05.01.01's enumeration and a remote mixing listing publishes with no turnaround. A buyer orders it; the requirements gate passes; 05.01.06's Running state has no duration to commit and no due date to render, so the SLA state machine has no Estimated -> Running transition — while 05.01.06 asserts this state is unreachable.

findings.claim: 05.01.04 hardcodes its own facet-relaxation order (region, then genre) rather than reading the declared relaxation rank that 05.01.02 D-11 introduces specifically so browse and benchmarking cannot diverge, and it omits the 3-step relaxation cap that browse applies.
findings.evidence: 05.01.04-rate-benchmarking-price-transparency.md:45 — "| Cohort below minimum size (cold start — the normal case at launch) | Band suppressed; progressively relax facets (**drop region, then genre**) and label the relaxation |", repeated at :31 and in the Relaxed state at :64 ("Cohort met only after dropping facets (region, then genre)"). CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:174 — "| D-11 | Each facet declares a **relaxation rank** as curated data; browse and benchmarking both read it | DT-11, closing 05.01 CX-08. Two independent orders drift silently, and the drift makes a rate band describe results it is not computed from." 05.01.02:143 flags the gap without tracking it: "Step 6 should confirm `05.01.04` consumes the rank rather than implementing its own." 05.01.04 never mentions D-11 or the relaxation rank. Browse also caps relaxation at 3 steps (05.01.02:89 "**max 3 steps**"); 05.01.04 states no cap.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether benchmarking reads the curated relaxation rank or its own fixed order, and whether it stops after 3 relaxation steps.
findings.failureScenario: A curator sets the declared relaxation rank so mode relaxes before region. Browse drops mode and returns remote cellists nationwide; the band beside them still relaxed region first and is computed over Leeds cellists. The buyer sees a price band that does not describe a single listing on the page — precisely the silent drift D-11 was written to prevent.

findings.claim: 05.01.07's waitlist behaviour is stated two incompatible ways in the same file: a sequential one-at-a-time offer with a 24h window that is explicitly 'not a first-to-click free-for-all', and a happy path in which the first waitlisted buyer to convert takes the slot.
findings.evidence: 05.01.07-seller-capacity-queue-intake-limits.md:32 — "**Waitlist as an ordered queue, not a scramble.** When a slot frees, the platform notifies waitlisted buyers **in join order**, one at a time, each with a bounded window to convert (Level-1 default: 24h) before the offer passes to the next. It is **not a first-to-click free-for-all**, because that punishes the buyer who was there first and rewards whoever happens to be online." CONTRADICTED BY 05.01.07-seller-capacity-queue-intake-limits.md:42 — "5. Waitlisted buyers are notified in order; **the first to convert takes the slot**".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a freed slot is offered exclusively to one waitlisted buyer at a time or broadcast to the queue with the first conversion winning.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the happy path: all waitlisted buyers are notified 'in order' and race. The buyer at position 1 is asleep, position 4 converts in 90 seconds, and the mechanism the Behavior section says exists — a 24h exclusive window per position — never runs. Position 1 is told they were on a waitlist that did nothing for them.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX identifies a sealed-anonymity + union-session combination as internally contradictory and 'likely illegal', leaves it unconfirmed, and assigns it no owner and no deferral target. No open question in 05.02.02 or 05.02.03 covers it.
findings.evidence: 05.02-quotes-scope-contracting-cx.md:13 — "| CX-04 | [05.02.02 NDA] | [05.02.03 Union] | A sealed union session is internally contradictory — the union must be told who played | Musician | Medium | A union session's whole point is reported, scale-paid, pension-accruing work. Sealing the credit defeats the reporting duty (02). **Likely an illegal combination; not yet confirmed.** |". 05.02.02's Q-01 (:122) covers only "Can a sealed engagement use a co-ownership or points posture at all?"; 05.02.03's Q-01..Q-04 (:96-99) cover scale-table sourcing, new-use, non-signatory buyers and launch jurisdictions. Neither file's edge-case table mentions the combination.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the anonymity elector must block, warn on, or permit Sealed on a union-elected engagement.
findings.failureScenario: A fixer elects Sealed on a union string date. Acceptance emits a suppressed credit per 05.02.02 D-01, and 05.02.03's step 6 emits session data to domain 02 for B-form reporting, which names every player. The platform simultaneously holds a credit it promised not to display and files a union report that displays it — the seller paid for anonymity that the same acceptance transaction destroys.

findings.claim: The unanswered-counter notification rule fires at fixed offsets of 24h and 2h before expiry, but expiry is seller-settable down to 1 hour and the file's own worked example uses a 2-hour expiry — so the rule is unsatisfiable on exactly the case it is written against.
findings.evidence: 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:125 — "| **Buyer counters at hour 1 of a 2-hour expiry; seller replies at hour 3** | The offer lapsed while the seller was writing. ... But a seller sitting on an unanswered counter loses the deal silently, so: notify the seller at **24h and 2h** before expiry when an unanswered counter exists. |" CONTRADICTED BY 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:235 — "| D-06 | **Default expiry is 14 days**; seller-settable from 1 hour to 90 days ... The floor is 1 hour, not 24, because emergency cover (05.05.01) is a real shape and a floor would kill it (DT-08)."
findings.forcedInvention: What the counter-notification schedule is when the quote's total lifetime is shorter than the notification offsets — skip, fire immediately, or scale to a fraction of the window.
findings.failureScenario: An emergency-cover quote is issued with a 1-hour expiry. The buyer counters at minute 10. Both notification offsets are already in the past, so under a literal implementation no notification is scheduled at all and the seller — the one case the rule exists for — is never told a counter is waiting. The offer lapses in 50 minutes and the date is uncovered.

findings.claim: 05.03.06 D-03 requires the recall window to be bounded in both duration and count, but no value or range is given for either, and only the duration is carried by an open question — the count bound has no tracked owner anywhere.
findings.evidence: 05.03.06-post-delivery-support-recall.md:89 — "| D-03 | The window is bounded in both duration and count | Otherwise it is unlimited revisions with extra steps (05.03.03 DT-01). |". The only tracked question is 05.03.06:99 — "| Q-04 | Default window length per craft? A mastering recall window and an album-mix recall window are not the same duration. | User | Step 5 deepening |" — duration only. The count appears once, as illustrative UI copy at :47 — "| Buyer uses recalls as free revisions | The abuse mode. Bounded count + scale test. | \"Recall 2 of 2 used.\" |" — with no stated default, floor, ceiling or per-craft table, unlike the equivalent tables 05.03.03 gives for revision rounds (:65-79) and 05.04.01 gives for auto-accept windows (:60-69).
findings.forcedInvention: The recall count bound: its default, whether it is per-craft, seller-settable, and whether the platform imposes a floor or ceiling.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer defaults the recall count to 1 to be safe. A mastering engineer's buyer uses their single recall on a trivial fade fix, then the vinyl cut comes back needing a different low end — the canonical recall the feature exists for — and the buyer is told the window is exhausted, so the work leaves the platform as an off-platform favour with no record, which is exactly the leakage 05.03.06 D-02 frames the feature to prevent.

findings.claim: 05.04.01 states that a revision request decrements the revision allowance; 05.03.03, which owns the allowance, decides the opposite and explicitly names the request-time decrement as a corrected error.
findings.evidence: 05.04.01-delivery-acceptance-auto-accept.md:113 — "| **Buyer requests a revision** | Window stops; engagement re-enters revision (05.03.03); **allowance decrements** | \"Auto-accept paused — {seller} has your notes\" |". CONTRADICTED BY 05.03.03-revisions-limits-change-orders.md:221 — "| D-09 | **The allowance decrements at redelivery, not at request** | A withdrawn round, a returned round and a wholly change-ordered round all cost the buyer nothing, because no redelivery happened. See DT-08. **Corrects the surface pass.** |", reinforced at 05.03.03:86 — "Round shows `2 of 3 remaining` (**not yet decremented** — DT-08)" and :111 — "| Buyer withdraws a round before the seller redelivers | Free. Nothing was consumed (DT-08). ... \"Round withdrawn — you still have 3 of 3.\" |".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether opening a revision round consumes an allowance unit immediately or only on redelivery.
findings.failureScenario: The delivery surface decrements on request per 05.04.01. A buyer opens round 3 of 3, the seller converts the whole round into a change order (05.03.03:112, which says 'No round consumed'), and the buyer is now at 0 of 3 — so their next in-scope note is routed to a paid change order they should not have to buy. The seller has monetised a round they never worked, which is the outcome D-09 was written to remove.

findings.claim: A single control-table cell in 05.04.01 both answers the working-days jurisdiction question and instructs that this feature must not answer it, while the question it cites is still open with no decision recorded.
findings.evidence: 05.04.01-delivery-acceptance-auto-accept.md:56 — "| **Business days** | The seller's jurisdiction's, per 05.01.06 Q-02, which owns this question. This feature inherits whatever that resolves to and must not answer it independently |". The cited question is unresolved: 05.01.06-turnaround-rush-service-levels.md:105 — "| Q-02 | Are \"working days\" the seller's jurisdiction's or the buyer's? They differ, and the answer determines who absorbs a bank holiday. | User | Step 5 deepening |". 05.01.06's own edge case at :52 leans the other way — "Due date is recomputed against **the buyer's timezone** and the governing holiday calendar (Q-02) at clock-start, then frozen".
findings.forcedInvention: Which jurisdiction's business-day calendar resolves the auto-accept window's floor (3 business days) and its per-craft defaults (5/7/14 business days).
findings.failureScenario: A UK seller delivers to a US buyer on the Friday before the late-May UK bank holiday. Under the seller's calendar the 5-business-day window ends Friday 6 June; under the buyer's it ends Thursday 5 June. Auto-accept executes a copyright assignment by silence on one of those two days, and the two parties were shown different absolute deadlines for the same window.

findings.claim: The requirement for a per-payee escrow freeze — rather than a whole-escrow freeze — when a downstream worker disputes while the buyer's acceptance fires is marked with a bare `[PENDING]` in two separate CX files, with no owner and no deferral target, and no open question in 05.05 or the domain index covers it.
findings.evidence: 05.05-multi-party-supply-cx.md:73 — "5. **State transition conflict**: A downstream engagement disputed while the buyer's acceptance fires. The buyer's release should not be held hostage to a dispute between the fixer and one player — but the disputed player's tranche must be. **Needs a per-payee freeze rather than a whole-escrow freeze; `[PENDING]`.**" Repeated at services-marketplace-cx.md:104 — "The buyer's release must not be hostage to a fixer-player dispute, but the disputed tranche must be — needing a **per-payee freeze**, not a whole-escrow freeze. `[PENDING]`." 05.05's open questions (:53-55) cover the credit counterparty, margin disclosure and entity sellers only; 05.05.02's Q-01..Q-03 cover margin, roster visibility and off-platform players.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a downstream dispute freezes the whole escrow release or only the disputed payee's tranche, and who decides.
findings.failureScenario: One of twelve string players disputes their fee with the fixer on the morning the buyer accepts. Under the only freeze mechanism the corpus otherwise specifies (05.04.01: 'Escrow frozen; routed to domain 24'), the buyer's entire release freezes, so eleven players who did their job and the fixer are unpaid over someone else's argument — reproducing the exact profession-old failure 05.05.02 D-02 and CX-05 exist to fix.

findings.claim: 05.05.04's mid-chain cancellation settlement and its `Broken` terminal state are both bare `[PENDING]` with no owner and no deferral target, and none of the feature's three open questions covers either.

The file's open questions (:102-104) are Q-01 (assembler vs platform as counterparty), Q-02 (cross-seller SLA attribution) and Q-03 (assembler margin disclosure) — none reaches settlement or the Broken state. findings.forcedInvention: The settlement arithmetic and terminal state when a four-seller bundle is cancelled or a mid-chain seller exits — including whose kill-fee schedule applies to each of the four unsettled stages.
findings.failureScenario: A buyer cancels a tracking+mix+master+artwork bundle after stage 2. 05.03.05's settlement engine expects one seller and one declared kill-fee schedule; here there are four schedules, three of which belong to sellers who have done nothing. The engagement enters `Broken` with no defined behaviour, and the escrow — captured whole at purchase per 05.05.04:37 — has no rule for splitting across four parties.

findings.claim: What happens to an elected points participation when the recording is later re-recorded is marked with a bare `[PENDING]` — no owner, no deferral target — and none of 05.06.02's four open questions covers it.
findings.evidence: 05.06.02-producer-points-backend-participation.md:62 — "| Points on a recording later re-recorded | The 2020s' favourite manoeuvre | `[PENDING]` |". 05.06.02's open questions (:122-125) are Q-01 (allow points-only at all), Q-02 (block an unauthorised grant), Q-03 (where the aggregate check lives pre-recording) and Q-04 (show an honest expected value) — none addresses re-recording. 05.06.03, which owns execution and models the departed-party and moved-allocation cases explicitly (:145), does not cover it either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a producer's executed master-points participation attaches to the specific recording only, or follows a re-recording of the same composition — and what the platform records at 09/10 when a buyer re-records precisely to shed the participation.
findings.failureScenario: A producer takes 3 master points and no fee. Two years later the artist re-records the track and releases the new master. 09 holds a participation against a recording that is no longer exploited and no participation against the one that is; domain 10 collects nothing, and the platform's flagship 'binding rights transfer' has produced a registered interest in a shelved asset — the outcome 05.06.02 D-02 ('a recorded promise is what the industry already has') exists to prevent.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether a recalled and redelivered master requires a fresh clearance and human-performance declaration, and what the buyer relies on in the interval.
findings.failureScenario: A mix is accepted with an 'Original' clearance declaration; the transfer executes. Inside the recall window the seller redelivers a corrected mix that now contains a library loop under a no-sync licence. No gate fires (D-07 covers revisions, not recalls), no acceptance re-executes, and the archived warranty describes a file the buyer no longer holds — so the buyer's only evidential protection is attached to a superseded artifact at the exact moment it matters.

findings.claim: Two custody-chain precedence races — damage discovered at return while the job is still in progress, and a revised estimate issued while the item is already being returned — are marked with a bare `[PENDING]` in the sub-domain CX, with no owner and no deferral target, and no open question in 05.07.01 or 05.07.03 covers either.
findings.evidence: 05.07-custodial-physical-services-cx.md:41 — "5. **State transition conflict**: Damage discovered at return while the job is still marked in progress; or a revised estimate issued while the item is already being returned. **Both need a defined precedence; `[PENDING]`.**" 05.07.01's open questions (:116-119) cover return shipping on a declined estimate, abandoned items, diagnostic fees and the reassembly state on a declined revised estimate; 05.07.03's (:115-118) cover seller insurance, declared value from 15, the vintage-refret warning and orphaned items. Neither file's States table (05.07.01:65-77, 05.07.03:69-77) defines an ordering between `In Progress`, `Revised Estimate`, `In Transit (return)` and `Disputed`.
findings.forcedInvention: Which event wins when a return-leg condition record and a live job state conflict — i.e. whether the custody comparison runs against the intake+approved-estimate specification as it stood at dispatch or as amended mid-return.
findings.failureScenario: A tech dispatches a repaired guitar, then issues a revised estimate for extra work discovered during final setup. The buyer receives the instrument and files a condition delta. Under 05.07.03 D-04 the delta is measured against 'intake + approved estimate'; with an unapproved revision in flight there are two candidate specifications of permitted change, and the same physical fact reads as authorised work under one and as damage under the other — with escrow frozen either way.
